muscarinic blockade by atropine sulfate has no effect upon the sensorimotor EEG of cats during sleep or waking immobility but does reduce the frequency content of this EEG during movement.
atropine does affect the EEG, but not in a way that is consistent with the idea that it is a "generalized CNS depressant" and not at all in a way that supports a "generalized arousal" hypothesis.

the sensorimotorsystem is not controlled by a single system.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of atropine on the EEG are state-dependent.
atropine does not affect the sensorimotor EEG in a uniform manner.
